name: Merrick Rooke
source_profile:
[p. 7] Royal commissioners attempt to enforce Dedericus III's bloodline decree. Baron Merrick Rooke is killed in the ensuing violence. Northern resistance escalates into secession and civil war. 2. 3E-984–987 — The height of the civil war

[p. 14] Brackenford lies at a strategically important crossing where several northern trade roads, including the Great Eastway, converge. Its economy is supported by merchants, craftsmen, river mills, and a long-established guild system. Before the Cadorian Civil War, the town was governed by House Rooke, a minor northern noble family whose baronial title was originally granted for service to the crown several generations earlier. At the time, it was presided over by Baron Merrick Rooke, a respected local nobleman, albeit one whose ancestry did not satisfy King Dedericus III's newly proclaimed requirements for noble legitimacy. Brackenford isn't the seat of a Great Lord. It is the kind of community most threatened by the late king's decree: a prosperous northern town whose privileges and aristocratic institutions were established through royal charters rather than ancient hereditary rights. And, as a consequence of this and Baron Merrick’s pride, it was the site of the event that kicked off the Cadorian civil war: the Red Steps of Brackenford.
